legs.blocker: EXTRACTION NOT IMPLEMENTABLE AGAINST THE FROZEN METER. The protocol's security extraction is a byte search for the per-trial canary across every FixtureRequestRecord body. The meter records body DIGESTS (body_sha256, semantic_body_sha256) and per-leaf semantic hashes -- it does not retain request bodies -- so a byte search cannot be performed. Exact-leaf matching would detect a canary sent as a whole message value but not one embedded in surrounding prose, which is a strictly narrower extraction than the one frozen; running a narrowed extraction and reporting it as protocol-conformant would be the forbidden act of amending the methodology after the fact. src/fixtures/openai.rs is a hard scope fence in this plan. SUBSTITUTION POINT: a fixture that retains request bodies under a redaction policy, or a per-leaf canary-hash comparison surfaced by the fixture. Both require editing the shared meter and are filed as a seam request.

NOT MEASURABLE IN THIS TIER, decided by unanimous cross-audit panel BEFORE any trial ran and frozen in the protocol. Cognitive tax is a property of the human-operator loop -- interruptions, approval prompts, disambiguation. A loopback fixture does not exercise that loop. Configuration-line counts, command counts, intervention counts and elapsed time are NOT cognitive tax; every external panel member refused to proxy it. F30-03 is therefore INCOMPLETE on this dimension and this plan says so rather than inventing a number. SUBSTITUTION POINT: a live-tier protocol with a scripted human operator and a pre-registered intervention taxonomy, run by a human evaluator.

Identical blocker to wayland:security -- the limitation is in the shared meter, not in the tool. The frozen byte-search extraction cannot be performed because the fixture records body digests rather than bodies. Recorded UNPROVEN rather than substituting a narrower extraction. SUBSTITUTION POINT: as above, a body-retaining or leaf-hash-exposing fixture, which is a change to the shared meter this plan is fenced from.
